result.title: Closing the Modality Gap via Simplex-Constrained Representations
result.summary: While multimodal contrastive models like CLIP and CLAP successfully learn shared representations, their embeddings typically exhibit a persistent \emph{modality gap}. We propose addressing this separation through a purely geometric approach: changing the embedding domain from the unit sphere, $S^{d-1}$, to the probability simplex, $Δ^{d-1}$. Although both manifolds share the same intrinsic dimension, the simplex acts as a structural prior; its nonnegative, unit-mass constraints serve as a cross-modal calibration that forces both modalities to ground themselves in the same coordinate system. By attaching lightweight softmax adapters and using Total Variation similarity, we reduce the centroid $\ell_2$ gap by 97--99\% across five multimodal retrieval benchmarks. This confirms that simplicial geometry induces genuine semantic alignment, matching or exceeding the retrieval performance of standard unconstrained models.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将多模态对比模型（CLIP、CLAP）的嵌入域从单位球改为概率单纯形，附加轻量 softmax adapter，并用总变差相似度替代余弦，在五个检索基准上将质心 ℓ2 模态间隔缩小 97–99%，检索性能持平或更优。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文不涉及 latent 推理或证据使用，但把单纯形的非负、单位质量约束当作跨模态校准先验，并以 TV 相似度替代余弦，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度度量与视觉-语言状态对齐的几何选择。
